reasons: The finding is correctly characterized: Section 19.2 grants only a ninety-day Deliverable conformance window, which is the playbook fallback rather than the preferred twelve months, and because Deliverables expressly include configurations and integrations (Section 1.4) that may embed software (Section 13.2), the shorter window is a genuine gap against the preferred position.

The redline is minimal and surgical (changed-character ratio 0.145): only the duration phrase is altered, leaving the Hosted Services conformance, authority warranty, Section 19.4 remedy and Section 19.5 disclaimer carve-out intact.
Direction is correct and pro-customer — a longer conformance period increases Vendor obligation; the numeral-plus-word form ('twelve (12) months') removes ambiguity.

Rule coverage is complete: the rationale accounts for the workmanlike-manner warranty (19.1), documentation conformity (19.1-19.2), no malicious code and legal compliance (19.3), repair/replace/refund remedy (19.4), and confirms the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranties (19.5), so no additional insert is required.
Comment complies with tone and format requirements: prefixed, first-person plural, two sentences, cites the playbook position and offers the ninety-day fallback for non-software Deliverables.

The failing deterministic check ('warranty period ≥ 90 days … number not found') is a false negative — the edited text states 'twelve (12) months', which satisfies the months-expressed condition and exceeds ninety days; it does not indicate a substantive defect.
